questions.q: Why is the best cross-validated score from a large grid search usually too optimistic?
options: Cross-validation always uses the test set
The winner is chosen as the maximum of many noisy estimates, so it tends to be one that got lucky
Grid search trains on the validation folds twice
Larger grids always overfit the training data
questions.explain: Each combination's cross-validation score has random error. Selecting the maximum picks a score whose error is likely positive, and the effect grows with the number of combinations.

questions.q: In nested cross-validation, what does the outer loop do?
options: Tunes hyperparameters on the whole dataset
Repeats the final model fit with different random seeds
Selects which features to drop
Holds out data the entire tuning procedure never sees, and scores the tuned model on it
questions.explain: For each outer fold, a full grid search runs on the remaining data, and the winner is scored on the held-out fold. The average of those scores estimates how the whole tune-then-fit procedure performs.

questions.q: How do you run nested cross-validation in scikit-learn?
options: Pass a GridSearchCV object to cross_val_score with an outer cv
Call GridSearchCV with nested=True
Use the test set as the outer loop
It requires a separate NestedCV class
questions.explain: GridSearchCV is an estimator, so cross_val_score(gs, X_tr, y_tr, cv=outer) runs the whole search inside each outer fold.

questions.q: After nested cross-validation gives you an honest estimate, how do you build the model you will deploy?
options: Use any of the models fitted inside the outer folds
Average the five outer-fold models
Run a normal grid search on all the training data and use the refit winner
Retune using the test set
questions.explain: Nested CV is for estimating performance, not for building the model. Fit the final model with an ordinary search on all the training data.

questions.q: Which practice best keeps your final performance estimate honest?
options: Look at the test set after each tuning round to guide the next round
Use the largest search grid possible
Report best_score_ as your expected performance
Make all tuning decisions on training data and look at the test set once, at the end
questions.explain: Once the test set influences a decision, it stops being an independent check. Tune on training data only, and evaluate on the test set a single time.
